channel.title: InnotechInsider — Science
channel.description: Discoveries at the edge of physics, biology, energy, and beyond.

item.title: How Mathematicians Learned to Stop Panicking and Love AI
item.description: Sam Altman observed mathematicians pivoting from existential panic to routine adoption. Formal proof systems turned mathematics into AI's clearest sandbox.

item.title: How Claude Built De Novo Protein Binders to Neutralize Scorpion Venom
item.description: Anthropic has bridged generative reasoning and molecular biology, deploying Claude to engineer synthetic protein binders against lethal scorpion neurotoxins.

item.title: Neanderthal Wooden Tools Preserved in Stone Rewrite Human Tech Origins
item.description: Discovered in Spanish travertine, 60,000-year-old wooden artifacts encased in stone reveal sophisticated Neanderthal carpentry, upending deep technological history.

item.title: The Twilight Zone Paradox: A 10-Year Probe of Ocean Deep Reefs
item.description: Ten years of continuous autonomous data from the ocean’s mesophotic reefs are finally in. The verdict challenges everything we assumed about marine climate refugia.

item.title: Pennsylvania Measles Death Exposes America’s Digital Health Failure
item.description: A rare adult measles death in Pennsylvania lays bare the fatal convergence of plummeting herd immunity, fragmented health data, and algorithmic misinformation.

item.title: Medieval Parchment Is Unlocking the Deep Genomic History of Sheeppox
item.description: Microscopic scrapings from 800-year-old parchment manuscripts are revealing intact viral genomes, rewriting the evolutionary timeline of deadly livestock plagues.

item.title: NASA Roman Space Telescope Launch: Watch Guide and Why It Matters
item.description: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope brings a field of view 100 times larger than Hubble. Here is how to watch the launch milestone and what it reveals.

item.title: To Save a Space Telescope, Engineers First Must Save Its Rescuer
item.description: When a commercial servicing craft aimed at extending NASA's Swift telescope hit a propulsion glitch, ground control had to rewrite the orbital rescue playbook.

item.title: The Physics of the Screamer: Why Inline-Four Motorcycles Are Going Silent
item.description: Explore the high-RPM acoustics and firing intervals behind motorcycle 'screamer' engines. Discover why this mechanical masterpiece is facing extinction.

item.title: How DNA Sequencing and IoT Tracked a Fast-Food Outbreak to the Source
item.description: When a sudden foodborne outbreak hit Taco Bell, health officials turned to advanced genomic sequencing and IoT supply chain logs to pinpoint contaminated lettuce.

item.title: Uganda's Dual Viral Threat: A Stress Test for Global Health Tech
item.description: Uganda faces a dire public health crisis as a confirmed Marburg case emerges amid a raging Ebola outbreak, pushing its healthcare system to the brink. This unprecedented dual threat serves as a critical stress test for global rapid response capabilities and cutting-edge health technology.

item.title: Why Airliners Shed Their Weight: The Critical Science of Emergency Fuel Dumps
item.description: When an in-flight emergency strikes, pilots sometimes make the dramatic decision to dump thousands of gallons of fuel. This isn't wasteful; it's a critical safety maneuver rooted in fundamental aerospace engineering and structural limits, designed to protect lives on board and on the ground.

item.title: Europe's Space Ambitions Grounded: Another Crucial Mission Scrubbed
item.description: Europe's crucial Earth observation mission, Copernicus Sentinel-7, faced yet another launch scrub, signaling deeper systemic issues for the continent's commercial space sector. This repeated setback threatens Europe's geopolitical independence and its competitive standing against agile global rivals.

item.title: New Study Reaffirms COVID Vaccines' Heart Protection Amidst Evolving Virus
item.description: A landmark study offers crucial clarity, reinforcing that COVID-19 vaccines provide significant cardiovascular protection against the virus's damaging effects. This evidence decisively tips the scales, showing vaccination far safer for heart health than confronting the infection unvaccinated.

item.title: The Vulcan Paradox: Ranking Spock Portrayals by Real Neuroscience
item.description: Popular culture treats Spock as the archetype of pure logic. Cognitive neuroscience reveals why only one portrayal actually mirrors how rational brains operate.

item.title: Mach 39 and Beyond: Why Artemis II's Fiery Return Redefines Space Travel
item.description: Artemis II will push the boundaries of human spaceflight, testing the Orion capsule's ability to survive a scorching Mach 39 atmospheric re-entry from lunar orbit. This unprecedented speed isn't just a record; it's a critical crucible for the hardware and a vital precursor for sustainable deep-space exploration, defining the future of missions to the Moon and Mars.

item.title: Fusion's Second Shot: Why Repetition Rate Matters More Than Net Energy
item.description: Proving net energy gain was a triumph of physics, but the engineering race to fire fusion pellets multiple times per second is what will actually build a grid.
